recent_posts.title: Jan-Piet Mens :: A wiki from a single Go binary: LeoMoon Wiki-Go
recent_posts.summary: LeoMoon Wiki-Go is a single-binary, databaseless, flat-file wiki platform written in Go. It serves Markdown files dropped into a directory, includes an interactive Markdown editor, Kanban boards, link management pages, a REST API, and user/role management via YAML config. It requires no database and can be run as a standalone binary or Docker container.

recent_posts.title: Jan-Piet Mens :: Deploying SSH host keys and certificates with Ansible
recent_posts.summary: A practical walkthrough showing how to deploy SSH host keys and certificates to nodes using Ansible. The approach uses two community.crypto modules — openssh_keypair and openssh_cert — with task delegation to localhost so the SSH CA operations happen on the Ansible controller while the private key stays on the target node. A block with an always clause handles cleanup of the temporary local directory even on failure.

recent_posts.title: Jan-Piet Mens :: SSH certificates: the better SSH experience
recent_posts.summary: SSH certificates offer a significantly better experience than traditional public key authentication by eliminating Trust on First Use (TOFU), removing the need to distribute public keys to each server's authorized_keys, and enabling short-lived credentials with built-in expiry. The post walks through setting up an SSH CA using ssh-keygen, signing both user and host keys, configuring servers to trust the CA, and updating clients' known_hosts with a single @cert-authority line. Additional features covered include forced commands, source IP restrictions, principal-based access control, and PTY permission management. A proof-of-concept automation using a Python BottlePy HTTP server and the sshkey-tools library is also demonstrated for automated host key certificate distribution.

recent_posts.title: Jan-Piet Mens :: Providing zone transfers directly from Netbox DNS
recent_posts.summary: A new Netbox plugin called netbox-plugin-bind-provisioner enables zone transfers (AXFR) directly from Netbox DNS by implementing a small DNS server within Netbox. The plugin supports TSIG authentication, multiple DNS views, and Catalog Zones (RFC 9432) for automated DNS server provisioning. Configuration involves setting up TSIG keys and specifying views, after which compliant DNS clients can transfer zones on TCP port 5354. The plugin works alongside the existing netbox-plugin-dns and may eventually integrate Catalog Zone support natively.

recent_posts.title: Jan-Piet Mens :: Ansible lookup plugin for generating TSIG keys
recent_posts.summary: A custom Ansible lookup plugin solves the problem of generating TSIG keys for DNS servers. Standard Ansible lookups like random_string get re-evaluated due to lazy evaluation, making them unsuitable for reuse. The plugin generates BIND-compatible TSIG key files and returns components as a dictionary, ensuring idempotency. Generated files include a comment with colon-separated algorithm, key name, and secret for easy extraction and use with dig's -y option.

recent_posts.title: Jan-Piet Mens :: Notes to self: Semaphore-UI secrets
recent_posts.summary: Explores how Semaphore UI stores secrets in its database, including variable groups and key stores. Demonstrates that secrets are encrypted at rest using AES and stored as base64-encoded data in SQLite. Shows how to decrypt these values by examining the source code and using the access_key_encryption key from config.json. Emphasizes the importance of securing and backing up the config.json file since it contains the encryption keys needed to decrypt all stored secrets.

recent_posts.title: Rescuing data from an abandoned Proxmox server
recent_posts.summary: A technical rescue mission involving extracting data from an abandoned server running Proxmox virtualization. The process included dumping a QEMU container, mounting disk images, and migrating a MySQL database to SQLite format for easier access. The story highlights practical system administration skills and the use of tools like vzdump, mysql2sqlite, and DB Browser for SQLite in data recovery scenarios.

recent_posts.title: Jan-Piet Mens :: Blast from the past: Facit A2400 terminal
recent_posts.summary: A nostalgic look at setting up a vintage Facit A2400 terminal from 1989 for educational purposes. The author configures OpenBSD with serial console support at 19200 baud to demonstrate how developers worked with hardware terminals before modern computing. The setup involves configuring boot.conf and ttys files for serial communication, highlighting the technical challenges of connecting legacy hardware to modern systems.

recent_posts.title: Jan-Piet Mens :: Accessing KeePassXC password stores with an Ansible lookup plugin
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of using an undocumented Ansible lookup plugin to retrieve passwords and attributes from KeePassXC password databases. The plugin requires environment variables for the database path and password, and can access both the main password field and custom attributes using a specific naming convention with 'attr_' prefix.

recent_posts.title: Debian repository key rollover using multiple GPG keys in keyrings
recent_posts.summary: Debian 13 introduced stricter security policies that reject SHA1-based GPG signatures, causing issues with package repository verification. The author discovered that repositories can use keyrings containing multiple GPG keys, enabling smooth key rollover without breaking client installations. This approach allows maintaining both old and new signing keys simultaneously during transitions, avoiding the Catch-22 situation where clients can't verify updates due to changed keys.
